fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Jesus says, "The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs." (Luke 17:20) No countdown, no flashing arrow, nothing to squint at from the window. The Pharisees asked when the kingdom would come, and that's the answer Jesus gave them.

Jesus says the exact opposite, baker. He tells the Pharisees, "The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs." (Luke 17:20) So it won't arrive with observable signs. I'll be honest, I would have loved a sign too, even a tiny one shaped like a cookie.
Right there with them! Jesus says, "…the kingdom of God is in your midst." (Luke 17:21) He's telling this to the Pharisees. That's like the spatula that was in your hand the whole time.

That's what Jesus says, friend. "Do not go out or chase after them." (Luke 17:23) When somebody hollers "Look, there He is!", Jesus says not to go out or chase after them. No sprinting, no sneakers, no dust cloud.
Sending a scout sounds smart, I'll give you that. But Jesus says, "Do not go out or chase after them." (Luke 17:23) He doesn't talk about sending anyone.

A slow, steady picture is a nice thought, but it's not the one in this verse. Jesus says, "For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day." (Luke 17:24) Lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other.

That would be a nicer sentence, friend, but it's not the one Jesus says. He says, "But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation." (Luke 17:25) The word is rejected. I think it's a hard one to read.

Ordinary life, right up to the last minute. Jesus says, "People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark." (Luke 17:27) Nothing in that list is strange, it's everyday stuff. Noah is the one who entered the ark.

That's a serious scene, but Jesus doesn't paint it here. He says, "People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark." (Luke 17:27) Dinner and weddings are what He names. Noah is the one who entered the ark.

Jesus never mentions anyone helping with the ark. What He says is, "People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark." (Luke 17:27) Those are the everyday things Jesus lists, so I'd stick to them.

This one's the reverse, friend. Jesus says, "On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions." (Luke 17:31) So the person on the housetop isn't to come down to retrieve his possessions. I'd be tempted to run for my favorite mixing bowl, so I'm listening hard.

Noah is in this passage, so I see why you went there. But the wife Jesus names in this verse is a different one. The line is "Remember Lot’s wife!" (Luke 17:32) Lot is the one whose story He had just told.

Healing is a good guess, but it's not in this verse. He says, "…two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left." (Luke 17:34) Taken is the word. Two people, one bed, and one is taken.
